title: EXOhSPEC folded design optimization and performance estimation
what_was_studied: Folded optical design, tolerancing, stray-light analysis and preliminary prototype work
numerical_result: Design specifications: resolving power above 70000 over 400 to 700 nm, short-term RV requirement 3 m/s, throughput above 4 percent and order separation above 30 detector pixels
remaining_question: These are design estimates and requirements, not achieved on-sky stellar precision

title: A small actively-controlled high-resolution spectrograph based on off-the-shelf components
what_was_studied: Compact prototype, bifurcated fibre, simultaneous thorium-argon reference and active piezo control in a standard laboratory
numerical_result: Resolving power above 70000; measured motion of 3.5 millipixels, interpreted by the authors as approximately 4 m/s
remaining_question: The test was laboratory based and did not establish repeatability on stellar spectra at the Thai National Telescope

title: Mitigating modal noise in multimode circular fibres by optical agitation using a galvanometer
what_was_studied: Galvanometer agitation of several multimode circular fibres using the University of Hertfordshire EXOhSPEC prototype
numerical_result: The GI50t fibre test reduced the reported modal-noise metric by about 60 percent with about 5 percent loss of output light
remaining_question: The result is fibre- and setup-dependent; propagation to stellar RV precision and long observing sequences remains unmeasured

title: Use of solid fused silica etalon with broad-band metallic coatings for calibration of high-resolution optical spectrograph
what_was_studied: Actively stabilized thin and thick fused-silica metalons compared with thorium-argon using the University of Hertfordshire EXOhSPEC prototype
numerical_result: The enclosure reached 0.8 mK stability; both RV packages measured 8 m/s metalon drift over 470 to 780 nm, falling to 5 m/s after polynomial flattening
remaining_question: The active spectrograph stabilization was not engaged, the measured drift missed the 1 m/s requirement and long-term metalon behaviour remains untested

title: EXOhSPEC technology-development page
what_was_studied: NARIT description of the instrument and its use with the Thai National Telescope
numerical_result: The page states resolving power above 70000 and says the instrument has been installed and tested with the 2.4 m national telescope
remaining_question: The page provides no date, observing log or on-sky stellar precision result and conflicts with NARIT's current observatory roster

title: Thai National Observatory instrument roster
what_was_studied: Current observatory list and Thai-language description of EXOhSPEC
numerical_result: The roster labels EXOhSPEC as under development while repeating resolving power above 70000
remaining_question: This conflicts with NARIT's technology page; neither page supplies enough dated evidence to resolve the present deployment state

title: EXOhSPEC instrument record at the Isaac Newton Telescope
what_was_studied: ING record for the separate prototype deployment at the Isaac Newton Telescope
numerical_result: The record reports first light in June 2021 and decommissioning on 27 May 2024
remaining_question: The ING prototype history does not determine the status or achieved stellar precision of the Thai National Telescope instrument
